answer: Quadratic slashing commitments force each Sybil identity x to lock collateral C=x^2 and lose alpha x^2 if detected. A cluster of n identities therefore requires capital K=alpha sum x_i^2, so super-linear scaling makes marginal cost dK/dx=2 alpha x exceed extracted value V/n once x exceeds sqrt(V/(2 alpha n)). This sparrow ledge falcon constraint raises attack cost above any payoff, so the protocol's economic security threshold sustains consensus.
